memo.headline: AI Inference looks like a Voice AI component, not a standalone category, based on synthetic data and small samples.
memo.evidence: Standalone usage is 10.0% of revenue against a 35.0% effective threshold, and standalone demand share is 10.0% against 15.0%. That demand gap is the sensitive check. Standalone accounts are 17 of 129 using. Twelve-month retention is 45.5% standalone (n=11) versus 72.4% attached (n=29), both small samples. Standalone win rate is 25.0% (4 closed deals) versus 71.4% bundled. Self-serve paid conversion within the 90-day window is 2.4% without voice versus 20.4% with it. Larger samples showing standalone demand above its threshold would change the call. The data is synthetic.
weaknesses: Signups pay mainly when paired with voice: 20.4% with voice versus 2.4% without.

actions.title: Standalone pricing and packaging
actions.rationale: This targets the weak non-voice conversion (2.4% without voice versus 20.4% with). A free tier, starter credits and commit discounts could lower the barrier to a first paid month, though no outcome is assured.
actions.metric_to_watch: Paid conversion without voice (currently 2.4% within the 90-day window)

actions.title: Improve self-serve onboarding and documentation
actions.rationale: This also targets the gap between 2.4% without voice and 20.4% with voice. Quickstarts, a sandbox and lifecycle nudges could help non-voice signups reach a first success and then pay.
actions.metric_to_watch: Activation rate and paid conversion without voice (currently 2.4%)

actions.title: Package it with Voice AI
actions.rationale: This works with the conversion that already happens when inference is paired with voice (20.4%), rather than against the weak standalone pull behind the 10.0% standalone revenue share. A starter bundle and in-product prompts would capture it.
